The method trades a slight increase in residual error for fewer evaluations per vertex [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the method (iso_newton mode 2) predicts the next error and ends the vertex without an evaluation if the predicted error is below a tenth of the tolerance. It provides data showing a reduction in evaluations per vertex (1.3-2.0 instead of 2.0-2.6). It also notes that the largest vertex residual was 1.4e-4 h against a tolerance of 1e-4 h, indicating a slight increase in residual error (since the residual exceeds the tolerance, albeit slightly). Thus, the claim that it trades a slight increase in residual error for fewer evaluations is supported by the text.

The notes also confirm: 'Switch to ordinary 2D Newton iteration if K(X) ⊆ X AND ||I - M+ F'(X)|| < 1, as this guarantees exactly one unique solution in X and convergence.'
